title: Fireside Material Weathering Studio
description: A luxurious velvet sofa sits near a glowing pot of coals in a dim room. The user controls the heat intensity and proximity of the coals to progressively weather and transform the sofa's velvet material through stages — from pristine glamour to heat-scorched decay — while adjusting material properties like roughness, color shift, emissive glow, and normal map intensity in real time.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 (via importmap from cdn.jsdelivr.net) that loads PotOfCoals.glb and GlamVelvetSofa.glb using GLTFLoader. Scene setup: place the sofa at center, the pot of coals 2 units to its left on the floor. Use a PerspectiveCamera at position (0, 2.5, 5) looking at the sofa. Add OrbitControls. Lighting: one dim AmbientLight (0x1a1a2e, 0.3), one warm PointLight (0xff6600, 2, 10) positioned at the coals that flickers randomly in intensity (animate between 1.5 and 3.0). Add a subtle orange-red emissive glow to coal meshes. Create an HTML overlay panel with these controls: (1) a 'Heat Intensity' slider (0-100) that increases the PointLight intensity and changes its color from warm orange toward white-hot, (2) a 'Proximity' slider (0.5-3.0) that moves the pot of coals closer or farther from the sofa, (3) a 'Roughness' slider (0.1-1.0) that adjusts the sofa material's roughness, (4) a 'Scorch Level' slider (0-100) that blends the sofa's base color from its original velvet tone toward a dark charred brown (0x1a0a00) using color lerp, (5) a 'Emissive Heat Bleed' slider (0-1) that adds an emissive orange tint to the sofa material simulating heat absorption, and (6) a 'Reset' button that animates all parameters back to defaults over 1 second. Traverse loaded sofa meshes to access their MeshStandardMaterial and store original colors. All slider changes must validate min/max ranges and update materials in the animation loop. The flickering coal light should respond to Heat Intensity. Add a small text HUD showing current parameter values. Ensure the scene has a dark background (0x0a0a0f) and the floor is a dark plane with MeshStandardMaterial (roughness 0.9). The overall effect should feel like a dramatic material degradation experiment by firelight.
